## Oaks Analysis Outline

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Analysis Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

## Oak Data Input 

**Soil Moisture Data**

```{r}
Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")
```

**SPAD Data**

```{r}
SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")
```

**LICOR Data**

```{r}
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)
```

## Data Cleaning and Summary

**Soil Moisture Data**

```{r}
  #clean data
  Moist_Data <- Moist_Data_Raw |>
  
  #Remove rows without data
  filter(Treatment != "NA") |>
  
  #Convert VWC values of 0.0 to be NA
  mutate(VWC1_perc = case_when(
    VWC1_perc == "0.0" ~ NA, 
    VWC1_perc != "0.0" ~ VWC1_perc)) |>
  
  mutate(VWC2_perc = case_when(
    VWC2_perc == "0.0" ~ NA, 
    VWC2_perc != "0.0" ~ VWC2_perc)) |>
  
  mutate(VWC3_perc = case_when(
    VWC3_perc == "0.0" ~ NA, 
    VWC3_perc != "0.0" ~ VWC3_perc)) |>
  
  #remove rows that do not include any VWC data
  
  
  #remove columns that do not include data relavent for my analysis
  select(Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |>
  
  #change VWC  and date data into numeric values
  mutate(VWC1_perc = as.numeric(VWC1_perc)) |>
  mutate(VWC2_perc = as.numeric(VWC2_perc)) |>
  mutate(VWC3_perc = as.numeric(VWC3_perc)) |>
  
  #add average VWC as new column
  rowwise()|>
  
  mutate(VWC = mean(c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    
  #arrange by block and treatment to make reading easier
  arrange(Block, Treatment) |>
    
  #remove native recruits for consistency across data
  filter(Treatment != "NR") |>
    
  #remove empty row
  filter(VWC != "NaN")

  #check for any strange outliers/incorrect data
  Moist_Data |>
  summary(df$variable)

  Moist_Data
```

**SPAD Data**

```{r}
SPAd_Data <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> 
  
  #Remove rows without data
  filter(Treatment != "NA") |>
  
  #Remove columns not needed for my analysis
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, Dead_Alive, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6, Num_leaves, Notes)


  #Create dataframe with only observations of live seedlings
  SPAD_Data_Alive <- SPAd_Data |>
  
  #remove dead observations
  filter(Dead_Alive == "Alive") |>
  
  #select leaf observations and relavent ID data
  select(Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6) |>
  rowwise() |>
  
  mutate(SPAD_Avg = mean(c(Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6), na.rm = TRUE) ) |>
    
  arrange(Block, Treatment) |>
    
    #remove Native recruits for consistency across data sets 
    filter(Treatment != "NR")

  SPAD_Data_Alive
```

**LICOR Data**

```{r}
LICOR_Data <- LICOR_Data_Raw |>
  #Remove rows without data
  filter(Treatment_NA_NA != "NA") |>
  
  filter(Treatment_NA_NA != "??") |>
  
  #remove native recruits for consistency across data sets
  filter(Treatment_NA_NA != "NR") |>

  #Select data that we need for analysis
  select("USERDEF_Block Number_NA", "USERDEF_Tag Number_NA", 
         "Treatment_NA_NA", "Dead_Alive_NA_NA", "PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1", 
         "PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1") |>
  
  #rename columns with untidy names
  rename(Block_Num = "USERDEF_Block Number_NA") |>
  rename(Tag_Num = "USERDEF_Tag Number_NA") |>
  rename(Treatment = "Treatment_NA_NA") |>
  rename(Dead_Alive = "Dead_Alive_NA_NA") |>
  rename(Conductance = "PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1") |>
  rename(Transpiration = "PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1") |>
  
  #make data values of interest numeric
  mutate(Conductance = as.numeric(Conductance)) |>
  mutate(Transpiration = as.numeric(Transpiration)) |>

  #Combine observations from same sapplings as avg of measurements
  group_by(Tag_Num) |>
  mutate(Conductance = mean(Conductance)) |>
  mutate(Transpiration = mean(Transpiration)) |>
  distinct(Tag_Num, .keep_all = TRUE) 

LICOR_Data 
```

**Combine SPAD and Moisture Data**

```{r}
SPAD_Moist_Data <- left_join(SPAD_Data_Alive, Moist_Data) |>
  select(Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, SPAD_Avg, VWC) |>
  #remove unpaired values
  filter(VWC != "NA")

SPAD_Moist_Data 
```

**Combine LICOR and Moisture Data**

```{r}
Moist_LICOR <- left_join(LICOR_Data, Moist_Data) |>
  distinct(Tag_Num, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Conductance, Transpiration, VWC)

Moist_LICOR
```

**Combine all three data sets**

```{r}
##Need help/guidance. IDK what is happening here, joining either removes rows or creates NA Values. There should be a SPAD_Moist value for each LICOR. I have tried left_, inner_, and full_join. Full_join produces the most rows but with more gaps.  

All_Data <- left_join(SPAD_Moist_Data, LICOR_Data) |>
  select(Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, SPAD_Avg, VWC, Conductance, Transpiration) |>

All_Data
```

## ANOVA Test (Moisture by Treatment)

**Assumptions of Normality/Variance**

```{r}
#check general distribution trends by visualizing 
  Moist_Data |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = Treatment, y = VWC) +
  geom_boxplot()

  Moist_Data |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = VWC) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1.5)

#create model to test assumptions
  moist.lm <- lm(VWC ~ Treatment, data = Moist_Data)

#Shapiro test just to be sure
  shapiro.test(residuals(moist.lm))
  ##p=0.008; data not normal

#check homogeneity of variance 
  plot(moist.lm, which = 1)
  plot(moist.lm, which = 2)
  bartlett.test(VWC ~ Treatment, data = Moist_Data)
  ##p=0.599; variance rouhgly equal among treatments
```

By applying a Shapiro-Wilk test we see that the data is not normally distributed (p = 0.008). Nontheless, use of the Bartlett test demonstrates that the data is roughly equal in variance across treatment types (p = 0.599). We must use a non-parametric test; in this case the Kruskal-Wallis test.

**ANOVA**

```{r}
kruskal.test(VWC ~ Treatment, data = Moist_Data)

##Non-significant difference in soil moisture by treatment :(
```

**ANOVA Figure**

```{r}
#create summary stats anyways
  moist.summary <- Moist_Data |>
  group_by(Treatment) |>
    summarise(mean_VWC = mean(VWC), 
              se_VWC = sd(VWC)/sqrt(n()))
  
#create summary figure
  moist.summary |>
    ggplot() + aes(x = Treatment, y = mean_VWC, fill = Treatment) +
    geom_col() + 
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (mean_VWC - se_VWC), ymax = (mean_VWC + se_VWC)), width = 0.2) +
    labs(y = "Average Volumetric Water Content", 
         title = "Volumetric Water Content by Treatment Type")
```

## Regression Test (SPAD by Moisture)

**Assumptions of Normality**

```{r}
#visual data to identify trends
  SPAD_Moist_Data |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = VWC, y = SPAD_Avg) +
  geom_point()

#check distribution of both variables
  hist(SPAD_Moist_Data$VWC)
  hist(SPAD_Moist_Data$SPAD_Avg)
##VWC data looks bimodal/not normal. Use Spearman's Rank test.
  
#check for variance/homoscedasticity
  SPAD_Moist.lm <- lm(SPAD_Avg ~ VWC, data = SPAD_Moist_Data)
  plot(SPAD_Moist.lm)
  plot(SPAD_Moist.lm, which = 1)
  plot(SPAD_Moist.lm, which = 2)
  
  
```

**Regression Model**

```{r}
#r could not recognize columms, had to write test in weird way
  SPAD_Moist_Spear <- cor.test(~ VWC + SPAD_Avg, data = SPAD_Moist_Data, method = "spearman")
  SPAD_Moist_Spear
  
#isolate spearman coefficient
  rho_spear <- round(SPAD_Moist_Spear$estimate, 3)
  rho_spear
  #rho = -0.237

#isolate p-value
  p_spear <- round(SPAD_Moist_Spear$p.value, 3)
  p_spear
```

**Regression Figure**

```{r}
#view linear model
  SPAD_Moist.lm
  summary(SPAD_Moist.lm)

#slope of best fit line
  slope <- coef(SPAD_Moist.lm)[2]
  slope

#intercept of best fit line
  intercept <- coef(SPAD_Moist.lm)[1]
  intercept

#p-value for best fit line
  summary(SPAD_Moist.lm)$coefficients[2,4]
  ##Best fit line is not very good/does not represent significant relationship
  
#create graph with best fit line. dashed line to show not a good fit/significant relationship
  SPAD_Moist_Data |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = VWC, y = SPAD_Avg) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Volumetric Water Content (VWC)",y = "Average SPAD", 
       title = "Average SPAD Value by Water Content")
```

## Regression Test (LICOR by Moisture)

**Transpiration**

```{r}
#visual data to identify trends
  ##VWC data is clumped and varies by decimal points. How to acount/show this better?
  Moist_LICOR |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = VWC, y = Transpiration) +
  geom_point()

#check distribution of both variables
  hist(Moist_LICOR$VWC)
  hist(Moist_LICOR$Transpiration)
  ##looks mostly normal

#check for variance/homoscedasticity
  Transp_Moist.lm <- lm(Transpiration ~ VWC, data = Moist_LICOR)
  plot(Transp_Moist.lm)
  plot(Transp_Moist.lm, which = 1)
  plot(Transp_Moist.lm, which = 2)
  ##doesn't look great but isn't terrible?

#creat figure for model
  summary(Transp_Moist.lm)
  
  #slope of best fit line
  slope2 <- coef(Transp_Moist.lm)[2]
  slope2
  
  #intercept of best fit line
  intercept2 <- coef(Transp_Moist.lm)[1]
  intercept2
  
  #p-value for best fit line
  summary(Transp_Moist.lm)$coefficients[2,4]
  ##Best fit line isn't great/does not represent significant relationship
  
  #create graph with best fit line. dashed line to show not a good fit/significant relationship
  Moist_LICOR |>
  ggplot() + aes(x = VWC, y = Transpiration) +
  geom_point()+ geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Volumetric Water Content (VWC)", y = "Transpiration (mmol*m^2/sec)", 
         title = "Oak Transpiration by Soil Water Content")
```
